policy: Only official Mojo 1.2.0 standard library application dependencies. No third-party libraries, new native bindings, product subprocess helpers, code generation or Python runtime.
production_imports: std.sys._libc_errno (bundled errno classification and messages; no new binding)

unconnected_foundations.status: Native recovery policy is not connected to production recovery entrypoints. Recovery has native and pinned-source differential tests only. Quota handoff policy remains unconnected after checkpoint 13; no production recovery or admission claim follows from its component tests.
unconnected_foundations.assessment: Recovery policy remains unconnected to live goal recovery. All external imports are official Mojo stdlib.
unconnected_foundations.pointer_ownership: Recovery consumes owned Strings and the existing JSON document; no borrowed state escapes a synchronous call.

linker_inputs: Mojo default host link, no custom library or linker flags
runtime_origin: Official Mojo compiler support runtime plus OS C/C++ runtime; no product C/C++ logic or added bindings. Actual shared-library resolution audited with ldd/readelf.
development_tools: Git/GitHub CLI for checkpoints and read-only reference retrieval
Python 3.14+ standard library, including compression.zstd, for complex test orchestration and independent compressed vectors only
bubblewrap for isolated test filesystem/network namespace
integration_targets: Codex is an external integration target, never a product implementation helper. Tests replace only Codex/provider peers with synthetic stdlib harnesses; Modex itself is always the compiled native production binary. Real Codex distribution qualification remains blocked.

production_subprocess_invocations.executable: Codex selected from PRODEX_CODEX_BIN or PATH
production_subprocess_invocations.purpose: Codex integration target: resolve executable paths and PATH commands, skip pinned Prodex shims and legacy hashes, then run bounded version capture, hook-trust app-server stdio, and selected exec invocation through official stdlib posix_spawnp.
Native relay isolation/supervision; private env carries upstream key, bounded readiness channel, direct-child kill/reap and idle parent-channel EOF exit.

compression_implementation: Native Mojo frame, FSE, Huffman, sequence and incremental checksum logic. Numerical format parameters follow RFC 8878. No external codec implementation, codec library, subprocess or generated production code is included. tests/fixtures/zstd-noncanonical-huffman.zst is synthetic non-executable test data. The same native reader accepts file and memory sources; upstream log payload display caps decoded data at 128 KiB and requires complete frames.
compression_dependency_evidence: docs/evidence/zstd-link.txt; tests/test_compressed_sessions.py runs Modex with only platform and official Mojo runtime libraries mounted, without a Python runtime or external codec.
release_artifact_status: No release artifact; development build only
clean_runtime_evidence: tests/test_runtime.py verifies version output with only the executable, platform and official Mojo runtime libraries mounted. The upstream follow process tests use the same isolated filesystem/network setup with synthetic log files and no executable implementation helper; Python/Node/Rust/Prodex are absent from Modex's namespace. Scope: tested version, detached snapshot and file-follow paths on local Linux; no distribution or cross-platform claim.
distribution_gap: The development executable has an absolute toolchain RUNPATH. Relocatable packaging and official-runtime redistribution/licensing require separate verification.
platform_specific_implementation: Linux session file validation reads /proc/self/fd metadata through std.os.stat, comparing descriptor device/inode with before/after lstat. No new native binding; Linux only, and not a cross-platform claim. Numeric session time rendering reads OS TZif files from TZ, /etc/localtime or /usr/share/zoneinfo, without adding an application library.
unicode_width_implementation: Unicode interval tables are authored in Mojo. Production uses only the official Mojo 1.2.0 standard library, including std.builtin.globals and the bundled private std.collections.string._grapheme_break lookup. No runtime Unicode data files, code generator, added application dependency, external width/codec implementation, or copied implementation code. The frozen unicode-width 0.2.2 behavior references Unicode 17.0 UCD and Emoji 17.0 as independent sources; unmodified test inputs and provenance are recorded in tests/fixtures/unicode17/README.md and SHA256SUMS. Unicode-derived interval data is licensed under Unicode License V3; distributions must carry LICENSES/Unicode-3.0.txt and NOTICE.
log_implementation: Native Mojo detached log snapshots, general runtime/session streaming, upstream file following, text/JSON projections, credential redaction, strict base64 and numeric parsing, Unicode 17 character classification, and runtime policy log-directory selection. No external logging/parser/codec implementation or build generator. Broker feeds and terminal views remain unfinished. Four earlier redaction differences and stream_payload secret masking remain unapproved.
unicode_alphanumeric_implementation: Static Unicode 17 Alphabetic union General_Category=N interval data in Mojo, checked over all valid scalars against pinned independent UCD files. Final data is re-derived with tests/unicode_properties_derive.mojo (test-only native Mojo audit); no production generator, runtime data-file dependency, Rust code copy, new binding or application library. See UnicodeData.provenance.txt for the corrected authoring history. Unicode License V3 and NOTICE apply.
toml_implementation: Independently authored native TOML 1.1 document parser and policy validation. Product build/runtime uses only official Mojo stdlib. tests/fixtures/toml11 contains only pinned MIT-licensed conformance inputs, expected typed JSON, version manifests and license; no upstream runner, implementation or generator is included. Production does not load test files. The frozen parser's independent limits of 80 array/inline-table levels and 80 segments per local key path are preserved. Tests cover semantic trees up to 80-by-80 nested tables; complete resource-boundary equivalence remains unverified.
log_timestamp_implementation: Native Mojo parsing and local rendering of RFC3339 and frozen custom log timestamps. Reuses the existing calendar/TZif implementation; no Chrono code, external parser, process helper, binding or application library is included. Official-release comparisons and native tests cover fixed/variable fields, signed years, Unicode whitespace, fractions, leap seconds, DST and historical offset rounding.
upstream_follow_implementation: Native incremental file following uses official Mojo file/stat APIs, retained descriptors, /proc/self/fd identity checks and std.time polling. The bundled private std.sys._libc_errno wrapper classifies OS errors without adding a native binding. Source discovery retains at most 32 files; reads and partial-line buffers are bounded. Explicit disk recording bypasses live registry discovery as in the release. Without recording, live broker/direct-source registries still fail explicitly; terminal views remain unimplemented. No service or executable supplies missing behavior. Linux only; other targets unverified.
general_stream_implementation: Native Mojo combines runtime/session followers under a shared 32-descriptor budget with per-source reservations, 2/10-second discovery intervals and all transcript projections per record. Operational event classification and detail rendering are independently authored from the frozen behavior contract; endpoint display performs native URL path parsing without a library or helper. Exact tested format cases do not establish complete URL or stream equivalence.
json_number_implementation: Native JSON numeric conversion reproduces the release's default significand-then-decimal-scaling order and output notation, using only UInt64/Float64 arithmetic and official Mojo numeric primitives. It was derived independently from actual oracle outputs, including finite seeded values. No dependency implementation or power table was copied and no production generator is involved.
sha256_foundation: Independent native Mojo SHA-256 from NIST FIPS 180-4, with incremental hashing and non-destructive digest calculation. Production Codex discovery uses it only to reject the six legacy bundled-runtime hashes pinned in the 0.165.1 source. Numerical constants are specified by FIPS, not copied from a dependency implementation; Python hashlib supplies independent test-only comparisons. This does not establish general cryptographic readiness or file-descriptor identity pinning.
loopback_http_foundation: Native Mojo HTTP/1 GET and an owning incremental POST reader over official internal nonblocking POSIX socket wrappers, with numeric loopback-only admission, request validation, absolute deadlines, bounded headers/body/framing and Content-Length/chunked/EOF response handling. Standalone tests include a filesystem containing only the driver and platform/official Mojo runtime libraries, sharing the host network to reach the synthetic loopback server. DNS, TLS, proxies, redirects, general HTTP equivalence and live broker admission remain unfinished.
process_environment_foundation: Official stdlib posix_spawnp/dup/dup2/fcntl/Pipe support explicit env, selected argv0, bounded simultaneous stdout/stderr capture and startup-only stdio redirection. Production launch performs swaps before background work. Parent descriptors/flags restore on success/error. Signal forwarding, process groups, descendant cleanup and non-host targets remain gaps.
provider_sse_foundation: Independently authored native Mojo incremental byte framing and JSON assembly reuse the existing JsonDocument and Unicode trim helpers. Line/event/accumulation limits default to 4 MiB; framing returns at each complete event so callers can stop before trailing errors. The test driver stops at [DONE]. Only official collections/string facilities and local modules are imported; no pointer API, new binding, external parser or implementation helper is added. Native, fragmented-input and clean-runtime tests cover the standalone framing/assembly contract. The chat reader additionally has synthetic official-release adapter comparisons; neither is connected to the CLI. HTTP/TLS/proxies, backpressure/cancellation and complete transport/provider parity remain unfinished.
provider_chat_chunk_foundation: Native Mojo selects the first chat-compatible choice, decodes choice metadata/deltas and classifies embedded errors using the existing JSON decoder/serializer. Frozen-source projections preserve type, null and fallback rules; no foreign implementation, pointer API or new dependency is used. These helpers remain outside CLI/provider execution.
provider_chat_stream_foundation: Native Mojo composes incremental SSE framing/JSON assembly with DeepSeek-compatible response events, metadata/usage projection, tool argument accumulation and item conversion. The implementation reuses local JSON/text/redaction and only official stdlib APIs. UUIDv7 fallback IDs read 16 random bytes from /dev/urandom through the official file API and use the pinned stdlib realtime clock; failure is explicit, with no weak random fallback or new binding. RTK support rewrites command strings only and never launches RTK. Synthetic official-release fixtures compare adapter output to a standalone native driver, and the new guarded production Super tests check named live release observations. Complete auth/config, HTTP/TLS/proxies, persistent conversations, transport backpressure/cancellation and non-host platforms remain unfinished. No provider contract is PASS.
provider_request_foundation: Native Mojo composes Responses input/history translation, message adjacency/thinking normalization, function/custom/MCP/namespace tool translation, strict schema checks, request parameters/metadata and the frozen body-only simple-request conformance pass. Only official std.collections and existing local JSON/text/float code are imported; there is no pointer API, native binding, application dependency, implementation helper or build generator. Production builds do not load fixture data or invoke the Python test harness. Inputs/expected observations come from a checksum-pinned synthetic loopback oracle; source-derived native tests separately check pending message state and diagnostics. Request route selection/Anthropic web-search adaptation, credential/config handling, conversation storage/lookup, full HTTP/TLS/proxies, cancellation/backpressure equivalence, complete error/resource equivalence and general CLI dispatch remain unfinished. The guarded production Super slice now invokes translation. The bounded loopback transport subset is described separately. No provider contract or new platform obligation is PASS.
provider_transport_foundation: Native Mojo joins request preparation, source-derived header/auth filtering, an owning HTTP POST stream, incremental DeepSeek SSE and buffered JSON response translation. Its bounded retry and key rotation now run in the production Super relay. It reuses the bundled official POSIX socket wrappers and shared GET setup/parsing helpers; no new ABI, external application library, helper process, generator or Python production dependency is added. Socket and buffer storage outlive synchronous calls; moves retain one descriptor owner and close/drop/error paths close it. Complex Python stdlib harnesses serve only synthetic loopback peers and run the actual native driver, including a bubblewrap filesystem without implementation executables. Stored checksum-pinned request/SSE observations are replayed without changing their bytes. The connected path remains numeric-loopback-only with buffered bodies limited to 4 MiB and SSE decoded incrementally beyond that aggregate size while retaining 4 MiB line/event/JSON-accumulation guards. TLS/DNS/proxies/redirects/pooling, persistent conversation state, full backpressure/error/resource equivalence and non-host targets remain unfinished. No complete contract or new platform obligation is PASS.
provider_buffered_implementation: Native Mojo buffered chat JSON mapping reuses local JSON/usage/metadata/tool/UUID helpers and only official stdlib. A separately authored bounded diagnostic scanner reproduces source-derived Serde-style error categories/byte positions only when the frozen structural fragment scanner rejects or tool-search output requires strict JSON. Ordinary argument strings preserve the frozen structural acceptance behavior; exact captures retain that boundary. Missing call IDs use existing UUIDv7; response-ID fallbacks remain the caller responsibility. Missing/invalid created values now read the existing official stdlib realtime clock at buffered translation, preserving supplied unsigned timestamps and retaining the timestamp argument for caller compatibility. A pure assistant-message extractor preserves original tool-call IDs/provider fields and normalizes tool content for the conversation result; no store is written. Python only captures/replays checksum-pinned synthetic oracle fixtures and serves test peers. No application dependency, binding, helper, runtime data loader or production generator is added. Native mapper and real HTTP tests do not establish full provider/CLI, parser/resource, persistent state or non-host parity.
runtime_local_foundation: Guarded production Super reaches the real native relay. Numeric loopback HTTP buffered/SSE Responses and binary/query Chat Completions passthrough are tested through the actual CLI and both checksum-verified pinned Linux releases. Multi-key DeepSeek requests use an atomic round-robin cursor, with tested precommit HTTP and native Anthropic error retries, exact structured-error classification, and conflict rejection when concurrent requests assign one identity to different keys. Native first-event retry classification preserves the pinned case-sensitive `error` event gate: a top-level code on uppercase event type `ERROR` does not trigger rotation without an `error` member. The relay is serial; worker lanes, admission, TLS, DNS, general cancellation and non-host behavior remain gaps. Checkpoint 3 shares the native passthrough writer across Chat Completions/early Responses statuses, delivers 3xx SSE before EOF and applies source-traced text-header validation. Buffered errors retain the pinned 4 MiB guard. Checkpoint 4 rejects invalid Responses continuation identifiers before provider dispatch: resolved response/session/turn-state values use the pinned 1,024 UTF-8 byte and C0/C1 control rules. Live production comparisons cover 12 rejection vectors, five valid boundary/precedence vectors, eight simple combo-model selectors and buffered translation-time timestamp fallback. Full affinity ownership, persistent/profile-backed state and recovery remain unfinished. Checkpoint 5 encodes non-ASCII upstream path bytes using native String/StaticString and builtin chr only; no URL package, helper, binding or import is added. Checkpoint 6 reuses the existing Optional namespace to select unscoped Super history and scoped internal history; reviewed HTTP framing and call-ID worker sources add no imports. Checkpoint 7 reuses that relay header byte loop for buffered passthrough, matching the frozen ASCII header constructor without a new import or dependency. Checkpoint 8 removes found-state from the shared session resolver so blank primary headers fall through to later aliases before metadata/body fallback; no imports or dependencies change. Checkpoint 12 uses existing List/String operations for suffix-assembled whole-dot path normalization; validated address/credential guards and imports remain unchanged. Checkpoint 14 carries the existing buffered/SSE dispatch choice into the owned header writer to retain zero length for buffered bodyless replies. Checkpoint 15 advances the existing cursor after route and continuation checks but before Responses translation; malformed Responses JSON consumes once. Three-process sequential tests cover unsupported routes, malformed Responses JSON, response/session/turn continuation rejections, and empty-input web search in `auto`, `anthropic` and `openai_chat`. Malformed request-target syntax remains unqualified; the tested malformed Chat Completions JSON case passes through unchanged. Other invalid-body, target, and translation-time rejection cases remain unqualified. No import, dependency or public flag changes. SSE Transfer-Encoding and other runtime gaps remain visible.
super_preflight_foundation: Production clean-home launch runs native hook-trust JSON-RPC. Request writes use bundled socketpair/send(MSG_NOSIGNAL), keeping closed-peer errors recoverable without global signal changes. Codex version/app-server help probes remove CODEX_HOME and five TEST_CODEX_* variables; the existing text helper now applies the frozen 0.153.2 minimum, with 0.165.1 and 0.439.2 synthetic oracle checks for rejection, exact-boundary/leading-plus acceptance, nonzero-probe diagnostics and bounded-output errors. No dependency or binding was added. Twelve-second per-RPC deadline, 16 MiB stdout-line guard and direct-child cleanup remain. Full launch/config/storage/companion parity is blocked. Checkpoint 14's 0.439.2 initialize client version and source traces remain historical.
provider_rate_limit_foundation: Native DeepSeek request/token header projection reuses local time parsers and bundled official numeric/time APIs. Native tests and real relay fixtures cover both SSE/buffered headers, rounded utilization and numeric/RFC3339/compound-duration reset values. Frozen source was traced at 0.439.1; relay validation and guarded production CLI checks still do not establish a complete provider contract. Checkpoint 2 adds HeaderValue::to_str-equivalent HTAB/visible-ASCII validation and production non-2xx/stream-error comparisons; projection remains confined to successful Responses rewrites as in the pinned dispatcher.

connected_native_runtime.assessment: Guarded clean-home DeepSeek Super exec now invokes these native modules through src/main.mojo. The relay is the same native executable in a supervised child process, not an external implementation helper. Only bundled stdlib wrappers are used.

runtime_recovery_foundation: NativeRecoveryRetry and owned-thread/goal wire policy have native assertions and 407 pinned Mojo policy differential vectors. Accepted mutations do not become progress. Monitor, owned transport, affinity release, ambiguous outcome handling and mutation dispatch are unconnected; no live recovery PASS is claimed. Checkpoint 13 adds explicitly unconnected 0.439.2 quota signal eligibility and 1,600 current-pinned source comparisons; the old 407 wire-policy checks retain 0.439.1 provenance. No account pool, WebSocket, transport/recovery owner or new dependency is added.
super_launch_implementation: Native clean-home overlay, pinned-source Codex executable selection from PRODEX_CODEX_BIN/PATH, selected plus bundled DeepSeek model catalog/metadata/default budgets, explicit config/environment, version/hook preflight, supervised same-image relay and Codex exec. Path selection and raw child arguments match selected 0.165.1 native ELF controls; active shebang tests record a preflight/final interpreter-visible path mismatch for relative and symlink aliases. Release lock side effects, existing state and complete storage/config/companion behavior remain blocked. Context/compaction CLI overrides now use the pinned UInt64 fallback/clamping rules and reach native Codex argv; catalog defaults retain the baseline string-only exact-value lookup behavior.

checkpoint2_dependency_audit.scope: Log/gateway/session CLI fixes, quota ASCII validation and native Super token-limit configuration reuse existing local modules and official stdlib. Synthetic Python stdlib harnesses remain test-only. No runtime delegation, FFI implementation helper or paid provider request was introduced.

checkpoint3_dependency_audit.scope: Only existing HTTP stream constants/types and local provider modules are reused. Synthetic Python standard-library tests drive the production binary; no product helper, interop or code generator.

checkpoint4_dependency_audit.scope: Combo parsing and continuation identity checks reuse local JSON/text/collection APIs; buffered fallback time uses the already-listed official stdlib realtime clock. The production path remains native Mojo. Python stdlib scripts emulate only external Codex/provider peers and invoke actual production binaries. No product helper, runtime delegation or paid provider traffic.

checkpoint5_dependency_audit.scope: One native UTF-8 byte loop reuses existing String/StaticString/builtin chr operations; no import or dependency was added. Python stdlib peers remain test-only.

checkpoint6_dependency_audit.scope: Existing native history contexts and JSON/String APIs only. No reader/usage/format production change; unsafe parity claims rejected. Test-only Python stdlib peers and fuzz harnesses do not implement Modex.

checkpoint7_dependency_audit.scope: One existing native header loop now also filters buffered passthrough. Only existing List/String iteration and response writers are used; Python remains a test-only external peer harness.

checkpoint8_dependency_audit.scope: One shared native selection loop loses redundant state. Existing validation and namespace callers use the corrected result; isolated Python stdlib peers remain test-only.

checkpoint9_dependency_audit.scope: The existing native path byte loop adds six ASCII URL encoding bytes using current builtin Int/String operations. Both worker proposals are excluded. Python stdlib capture and synthetic peers remain test-only; URL 2.5.8 source is inspected only as a checksum-verified frozen-reference dependency, never linked into Modex.

checkpoint10_dependency_audit.scope: One existing String.replace call normalizes HTTP path separators after raw slash trimming. Existing numeric-loopback/credential guards and dot-segment denial remain. No imports or dependencies added; Python stdlib peers remain test-only.

checkpoint11_dependency_audit.scope: Existing native RPC/time, HTTP length and nonnegative 64-bit estimator operations only. No import or dependency changes; test-only Python peers and frozen-source Rust/Mojo checks do not implement Modex.

checkpoint12_dependency_audit.scope: Only existing native List/String/builtin operations normalize whole-dot path segments after suffix assembly. Validation and separated numeric socket address stay unchanged; Python peers remain test-only.

checkpoint13_dependency_audit.historical_evidence_policy: Descriptions naming 0.439.1 retain historical provenance; target repinning is not a new behavioral qualification.

baseline_evidence_policy: Each description and artifact retains its original version; 0.165.1, 0.439.5 and 0.439.1 observations are not automatically 0.439.2 behavioral verification.

continuation_binding_foundation.implementation: In-process DeepSeek relay hashes credential and endpoint identity, remembers accepted response/session/turn bindings with bounded in-memory maps, and validates them before subsequent dispatch. The passthrough SSE observer validates JSON incrementally with existing Mojo standard-library and local helpers.
continuation_binding_foundation.limitations: Persistence, multi-profile/account identity, full release/recovery semantics and general streaming/security equivalence remain unfinished. Numeric-position counters saturate at one billion.

process_shutdown_foundation: The official std.sys._libc.kill wrapper signals only the owned direct Codex child on relay failure; wait is bounded and escalates through the existing direct-child kill/reap path. Descendant process-tree termination remains unverified.

strict_tools_environment_foundation.implementation: The existing standard-library environment reader, loopback URL parser and DeepSeek strict-schema normalizer now feed the production relay for explicit strict beta routes.
strict_tools_environment_foundation.limitations: Config-only settings and public TLS/DNS beta routes remain incomplete. Full UTS #46 hostname normalization is absent; only its mappings to forbidden URL host characters are rejected. As in the release, the simple-request pass can preserve nested tool schemas unchanged.

web_search_mode_and_messages_audit.scope: Production routing and message conversion reuse the existing Mojo environment, JSON, text and collection code. Python remains confined to isolated test peers and CI checks.
